findings.title: Global motion guard disables functional progress feedback
findings.trigger: A browser tab, navigation, or operation is busy and the app is running with normal motion preferences.
findings.actual: The broad selector disables animations/transitions on all non-whitelisted elements and all pseudo-elements, so the tab spinner, browser loading line, busy dots, and pulse dots never animate.
findings.expected: Functional progress indicators remain visible and informative; only decorative motion is scoped away, with reduced-motion overrides for the indicators.
findings.smallestFix: Scope the rule to the illustration subtree or explicitly exempt functional progress indicators while retaining reduced-motion overrides.

findings.title: Expanded guide-video dialog does not trap or restore focus
findings.trigger: A keyboard user opens the MCP guide video expansion and then tabs, presses Escape, or closes it.
findings.actual: Only the close button receives autoFocus; there is no focus trap, stable labelled heading, or focus restoration to the opener.
findings.expected: Focus enters and stays in the dialog, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the expand button.
findings.smallestFix: Add opener/dialog refs, a focus trap, a labelled dialog heading, and restoration after button or Escape close.

findings.title: Bigger-context dialog lacks modal keyboard focus management
findings.trigger: The settings recommendation dialog opens and the user navigates by keyboard or screen reader.
findings.actual: The dialog has aria-modal but no initial focus, focus trap, Escape handling, or focus restoration to its trigger.
findings.expected: The dialog receives focus, supports Escape, keeps focus within the modal, and restores focus on close.
findings.smallestFix: Add dialog and opener refs, initial focus, Tab trapping, Escape close, and restoration to the trigger.

findings.title: MCP step replacement is not announced or focus-managed
findings.trigger: The user activates Next, Previous, or a reachable MCP stepper button.
findings.actual: key={step} remounts the new content, but focus remains on the old control and there is no live announcement or focusable current heading.
findings.expected: The new step is announced and focus moves to its heading or first actionable control.
findings.smallestFix: Focus a stable current-step heading after move or use a scoped polite live region, and expose the stepper current-state relationship.

findings.title: Custom radio groups omit arrow-key semantics
findings.trigger: The user reaches onboarding language, interaction mode, or zero-risk model choices with the keyboard.
findings.actual: Buttons are given radio roles but every option remains in the tab order and Arrow/Home/End navigation is absent.
findings.expected: One radio is tabbable and arrow keys move selection within the group.
findings.smallestFix: Use native radio inputs or implement roving tabIndex and radio-group keyboard handling.

findings.title: Language and model popovers lack required popup focus behavior
findings.trigger: The user opens either custom popup and navigates by keyboard.
findings.actual: Listbox/radiogroup roles are present without focus transfer, restoration, roving tabIndex, arrow navigation, or an inert background boundary.
findings.expected: The popup follows its role's keyboard pattern and closes with focus restored to the trigger.
findings.smallestFix: Implement the matching popup pattern with opener refs, keyboard navigation, focus restoration, and a modal/inert boundary, or use a native select for language.

No reachable interaction or state-feedback impact.

cleanAreas.note: Reduced-motion preference, document visibility, animation-frame cleanup, and runtime preference changes are handled.
Reduced-motion fallbacks disable animation, transitions, and smooth scrolling.
Saved MCP credentials remain read-only until explicit Replace credentials is activated.
Future MCP steps are disabled while busy or before the current step is reached.
Visible progress and retry/error states expose live or alert regions.
Account operations expose aria-busy and loading has a reachable retry action.

notes: Manual source review only at baseline 5401800; no tests, typechecks, scripts, runtime, app starts, commits, pushes, or delegation.
The primary motion finding concerns suppression of functional progress feedback by the global CSS selector, not decorative animation preference.
